कर्नाटक रनज्य क े  बेंगलूरु में स्थित यू.आर. रनव उपग्रह क ें द्र (यू.आर.एस.सी.)  उपग्रह प्रौद्योगगकी के गलए इसरो कन अग्रणी क े न्द्र है। यू.आर.एस.सी. अंतररक्षयनर् 
की संकल्पर्न, अगिकल्प, गवकनस, संगवरचर्, परीक्षण, प्रमोचर् एवं कक्षीय प्रबंधर् क े  गलए अंतररक्षयनर् प्रौद्योगगकी में अग्रणी है। अंतररक्षयनर् के गवकनस कन 
दनगयत्व होर्े क े  कनरण, क े न्द्र अंतररक्षयनर् के अगिकल्प, गवकनस, संगवरचर् एवं परीक्षण हेतु अपर्ी गगतगवगधयों एवं अवसंरचर्नओं क े  अर्ुरूप अत्यनधुगर्क 
प्रौद्योगगगकयों के गवकनस में लगन हुआ है। चनर दशकों की अवगध क े  दौरनर्, यू.आर.एस.सी. र्े िनरतीय रनष्ट्र ीय उपग्रह (इन्सैट) प्रणनली सफलतनपूवाक िनगपत की 
है, जो एगशयन-प्रशनंत क्षेत्र में सबसे बड़े घरेलू संचनर उपग्रह प्रणनगलयों में से एक है तथन िनरतीय सुद ू र संवेदी (आई.आर.एस.) प्रणनली िनगपत की है , जो 
संचनगलत िू-प्रेक्षण उपग्रहों के सबसे बड़े उपग्रह-समूहों में से एक है। िनरतीय उपग्रह-समूह सगहत र्ौसंचनलर् (र्नगवक), अगत महत्त्वपूणा रनष्ट्र ीय अर्ुप्रयोगों के 
गलए सनत उपग्रहों के उपग्रह-समूह के सनथ एक स्वतंत्र िनरतीय उपग्रह आधनररत क्षेत्रीय स्थिगत प्रणनली जल्द ही प्रचनलर्ीक ृ त की जनएगी। चन्द्रयनर्-1, मंगल 
कगक्षत्र गमशर्, चंद्रयनर्-3, एस्ट् र ोसैट जैसे क ु छ अन्तररक्ष गवज्ञनर् गमशर्ों र्े दुगर्यन िर में ख्यन गत प्रनप्त की है। यू.आर.एस.सी. द्वनरन आरंि गकए जनर्े वनले िनवी 
गमशर् अत्यंत चुर्ौतीपूणा हैं एवं र्वोन्मेषी प्रौद्योगगगकयनाँ गवकगसत करर्े तथन अंतररक्ष अन्वेषण एवं उससे आगे के गलए उन्नत आधनरिूत संरचर्न की िनपर्न 
करर्े क े  अवसर प्रदनर् करते हैं। 
U R Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) situated in Bengaluru of Karnataka State is the lead centre of ISRO for satellite technology. URSC 
is in the forefront of spacecraft technology towards conceptualization, design, development, fabrication, testing, launch and  in-orbit 
management of spacecraft. As a seque l to its mandate of spacecraft development, the centre is engaged in development of cutting 
edge technologies of relevance to its activities and infrastructures set -up for design, development, fabrication and testing of 
spacecraft. Over a period of four de cades, URSC has successfully established Indian National Satellite (INSAT) system, which is 
one of the largest domestic communication satellite systems in Asia -Pacific region and Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) system which 
is one of the largest constellations  of earth observation satellites in operation. NAVigation with Indian Constellation (NAVIC) an 
independent Indian Satellite based regional positioning system with a constellation of seven satellites for critical national  
applications will be operational sh ortly. The Space science missions like Chandrayaan -1, Mars Orbiter Mission, Chandrayaan -3, 
Aditya-L1 and Astrosat have received World Wide acclaim and put India in the global map while at the same time inspiring the Gen 
next. The future missions being unde rtaken by URSC is highly challenging and provide opportunity to undertake development of 
innovative technologies and establish the advanced infrastructure needed for space exploration and beyond.

AIR FORCE COMMON ADMISSION TEST (AFCAT- 01/2027) FOR FLYING BRANCH AND 
GROUND DUTY (TECHNICAL AND NON-TECHNICAL) BRANCHES/ NCC SPECIAL 
ENTRY/GATE SCORE ENTRY FOR COURSES COMMENCING IN JANUARY 2028 
Date for submission of Online Applications: 12 NOV 26 (1100 Hr) to 11 DEC 26 (2330 Hr) 
through AFCAT website https://afcat.edcil.co.in 
 
1. Indian Air Force invites Indian citizens (Men and Women) to be part of this elite force as Group 
‘A’ Gazetted Officers in Flying and  Ground Duty (Technical  and Non-Technical) branches. Online 
AFCAT examination will be conducted on 31 Jan 27 (Sunday). 
 
2.  Candidates are to ensure their eligibility for the examination, as follows: -  
 
2.1. Candidates applying for the examination should ensure that they fulfill all the 
eligibility conditions for admission to the examination. Their admission at all the stages of 
examination viz. Written examination and SSB test will be purely provisional, subject to their 
satisfying the prescribed eligibility conditions. If on verification at any time before or after the 
written examination or AFSB Test ing, it is found that they do not fulfil any of the eligibility 
conditions, their candidature will be cancelled by the IAF. 
 
2.2. Mere issue of Admit card/ Call up letter to the candidate will not imply that his/ her 
candidature has been finally accepted by Indian Air Force.

*Disclaimer. The vacancies indicated are tentative and subject to change without notice. Actual intake 
would depend on organisational requirements, various cadre control mechanisms, availability of training 
slots and actual number of vacancies accruing in January 2028. IAF reserves the right to ascertain final 
vacancies in each branch. No representation in this regard will be entertained. Two seats are reserved 
from Ground Duty (Non-Tech) vacancies for candidates holding LLB degree. 
 
 4. Type of Commission. 
   
 4.1. Permanent Commission (PC) for Men & Women. Candidates joining as PC 
officers would continue to serve till the age of superannuation in their respective branches as 
per their rank. 
 
4.2. Short Service Commission (SSC) for Men & Women. 
 
4.2.1. The engagement period for Flying Branch (Men and Women) SSC Officers is 
fourteen years from the date of Commissioning. 
  
4.2.2. The initial tenure for Ground Duty (Technical & Non-Technical) SSC Officers 
would be for a period of ten years. An extension of four years may be granted subject 
to service requirements, availability  of vacancies, willingness, suitability and 
merit. 
    
4.2.3. Grant of Permanent Commission (PC) (at a later date) would be considered 
subject to service requirements, availability of vacancies, willingness, suitability , merit 
and as per prevailing policies on the subject. 
 
4.2.4. SSC officers are not entitled for grant of pension. 
 
5. Eligibility Conditions. 
 
 5.1. Nationality. Candidate must be a citizen of India as per Indian Citizenship Act, 1955. 
 
 5.2. Age. 
   
 5.2.1. Flying Branch through AFCAT and NCC Special Entry:  20 to 24 years as on 
01 Jan 2028 i.e. born between 02 Jan 2004 to 01 Jan 2008 (both dates inclusive). 
Upper age limit for candidates holding valid and current Commercial Pilot License issued 
by DGCA (India) is relaxable up to 26 years i.e. born between 02 Jan 2002 to 01 Jan 
2008 (both dates inclusive). 
 
5.2.2. Ground Duty (Technical & Non-Technical) Branch: 20 to 26 years as on  
01 Jan 2028 i.e. born between 02 Jan 2002 to 01 Jan 2008 (both dates inclusive).   
 
5.2.3. Marital Status: Candidates must be unmarried at the time of commencement of 
the course and marriage is not permitted during training. A candidate who marries during 
the period of training shall be discharged and will be liable to refund all expenditure 
incurred on him/her by the Government.  
 
5.2.4. The date of birth accepted by the IAF is that entered in the Matriculation or 
Secondary School Leav ing Certificate or in a certific ate recognised by an Indian  
University as equivalent to Matriculation or in an extract from a Register of Matriculates 
maintained by a University. The extract must be certified by the  proper authority of the 
University or in the Higher Secondary or an equivalent examination certificate. No other 
document related to age like horoscopes, affidavits, birth extracts from Municipal 
Corporation, service records and likewise will be accepted.  
 
 
3 
 
5.2.5. In case the Matriculation/  Higher Secondary Examination Certificate does not  
show the date of birth, or only shows the a ge by completed years or completed years  
and months, in such cases a candidate must possess a self-attested/ certified copy of a 
certificate from the Headmaster/ Principal of the Institution from where he/ she passed 
the Matriculation/ Higher Secondary Examination showing the date of his/  her birth or 
exact age as recorded in the Admission Register of the Institution. 
 
5.2.6. Candidates should note that only the Date of Birth as recorded in the  
Matriculation/ Higher Secondary Examination Certificate or an equivalent certificate  on 
the date of submission of application  will be accepted by the IAF and no subsequent 
request for its change will be considered or granted. 
 
5.2.7. The candidates should exercise due care while entering their Date of Birth. 
If on verification at any subsequent stage, any variation found in their date of birth 
from the one entered in their Matriculation or equivalent examination certificate, 
will render them disqualified. No representation in this regard will be entertained.

https://afcat.edcil.co.in. Aadhaar Card is mandatory for online registration. Detailed instructions for

any information is found to be incorrect, the candidature is liable to be cancelled at any stage 
of the selection process.  Please verify the correctness of information entered in all the 
fields before proceeding with the “ Submit” option.  Applicants will not be able to edit

MEDICAL STANDARDS FOR AIR FORCE COMMON ADMISSION TEST (AFCAT- 01/2027) FOR

NCC SPECIAL ENTRY/ GATE SCORE ENTRY

General Instructions 
1. In this section, standardized guidelines for the physical assess ment of candidates for 
commissioning through AFCAT into flying and ground duty branches in the IAF are elaborated. The 
purpose of these guidelines is to lay down uniform physical standards and to ensure that the 
candidates are free of health conditions that may hamper or limit their performance in the respective 
branch. The guidelines enumerated in this section are meant to be applied in conjunction with the 
standard methods of clinical examination.  
 
2. All candidates during their induction should meet the basic physical fitness standards which will 
enable them to proficiently undergo the training and the subsequent service in varied climatic and 
work environments. A candidate will not be assessed physically fit unless the complete examination 
shows that he/ she is physically and mentally capable of withstanding the severe physical and mental 
strain for prolonged periods. The requirements of medical fitness are essentially the same for all 
branches, except for aircrew in whom the parameters for visual acuity , anthropometry and certain 
other physical standards are more stringent.  
 
3. The medical standards spelt out pertain to initial entry medical standards. Continuation of 
medical fitness during training will be assessed during the periodic medical examinations held at NDA/ 
AFA prior to commissioning. They are not exhaustive, in view of the vast spectrum of diseases. These 
standards are subject to change with the advancement in the scientific knowledge and change in 
working conditions of Armed Forces.  
 
4. Laboratory and Radiological Investigations for Special Medical Board 
 
4.1. Hematology: Complete Haemogram (Haemoglobin estimation, Total Leucocyte Count 
with Differential Leucocyte Count, Platelet Count). 
4.2. Hb Electrophoresis will be carried out in candidates for commissioning to exclude

estimation (Fasting and two hours after 75 g anhydrous glucose/82.5 g glucose monohydrate 
loading), Lipid profile.

4.5. ECG.

General Physical Assessment 
 
5.  Every candidate, to be fit for the Air Force, must conform to the minimum standards laid down 
in the succeeding paragraphs. The physical parameters should fall within the acceptable ranges and 
should be proportionate. 
 
6. The residual effects of old fractures/ injuries are to be assessed for any functional limitation. If 
there is no effect on function, the candidate can be assessed fit. Following categories should be 
meticulously assessed: 
 
6.1. Spine Injuries. Cases of old fractures of spine are unfit.  Any residual deformity of spine 
or compression of a vertebra will be cause for rejection.  
 
6.2. Nerve Injuries . Injuries involving the trunks of the larger nerves, resulting in loss of 
function, or neuroma formation, which causes pain significant tingling, indicate unsuitability for 
employment in flying duties. 
 
6.3. Keloids. The presence of large or multiple keloids will be a cause for rejection. 
 
6.4.  Surgical Scars. Minor well-healed scars for e.g as resulting from any superficial surgery 
do not, per se, indicate unsuitability for employment. Extensive scarring of a limb or torso that 
may cause functional limitation or unsightly appearance should be considered unfit.  
 
6.5.  Birth Marks. Abnormal pigmentatio n in the form of hypo or hyper -pigmentation is not 
acceptable. Localized, congenital mole/ naevus, however, is acceptable provided its size is <10 
cm. Congenital multiple naevi or vascular tumours that interfere with function or are exposed 
to constant irritation are not acceptable. 
 
6.6. Subcutaneous Swellings. Lipoma will be considered fit unless the lipoma  is causing 
significant disfigurement/ functional impairment due to the size/ location. Neurofibroma, if single 
will be considered fit. Multiple neurofibromas associated with significant Café-au-lait spots 
(more than 1.5 cm size or more than one in number) will be considered unfit. 
 
6.7. Cervical Rib . Cervical rib without any neuro -vascular compromise will be accepted. 
Meticulous clinical examination to rule out neuro-vascular compromise should be performed in 
such cases. This should be documented in the Medical Board proceedings. 
 
6.8. Cranio-facial Deformities. Asymmetry of the face and head or uncorrected deformities 
of skull, face or mandible which will interfere with proper fitting of oxygen mask, helmet or 
military headgear will be considered unfit. Ma jor deformities even after corrective surgery will 
be considered unfit. 
 
6.9. History relating to Operations.   A candidate who has undergone an abdominal 
operation involving extensive surgical intervention or partial/ total excision of any organ is, as 
 
32 
 
a rule, unfit for service. Operation involving the cranial vault with any residual bony defect will 
be unfit. Major thoracic operations will make the candidate unfit.

 Cardiovascular System 
 
11. Pulse. Persistent sinus tachycardia (> 100 bpm) as well as persistent sinus bradycardia (< 60 
bpm) are unfit. In case bradycardia is considered to be physiological, the candidate can be declared 
fit after evaluation by Medical specialist/cardiologist. 
 
12. Blood pressure. An individual with systolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 140 mmHg 
and/or diastolic blood pressure greater than or equal to 90 mmHg shall be rejected.  
13. Cardiac Murmurs . Evidence of organic cardiovascular disease will be cause for rejection. 
Diastolic murmurs are invariably organic. Short systolic mur murs of ejection systolic nature and not 
associated with thrill and which diminish on standing, especially if associated with a normal ECG and 
chest radiograph, are most often functional. 
14. ECG.  Any ECG abnormality detected at SMB/Recruitment Medical Ex amination will be a 
ground for rejection. Benign ECG abnormalities like incomplete RBBB, T wave inversion in inferior 
leads, T inversion in V1 to V3 (persistent juvenile pattern), LVH by voltage criteria (due to thin chest 
wall) may exist without any struc tural heart disease. Echocardiography should be performed in all 
such cases to rule out an underlying structural heart disease and opinion of Senior Advisor 
(Medicine)/Cardiologist should be obtained.  
15. Congenital Cardiac Anomalies. All congenital cardiac anomalies will be declared unfit. 
16.  Cardiac surgery and interventions. Candidates with history of cardiac surgery/ intervention 
in the past will be considered unfit. 
 
Respiratory System 
 
17. Pulmonary Tuberculosis.  Any residual scarring in pulmonary parenchyma or pleura, as 
evidenced by a demonstrable opacity on chest radiogram will be a ground for rejection. Old treated 
cases with no significant residual abnormality can be accepted if the diagnosis and treatment was 
completed more than two years earlier.  
 
18. Pleurisy with Effusion. Any evidence of pleural thickening will be a cause for rejection. At 
the time of appeal, these cases will be subjected to detailed evaluation with appropriate 
investigations by Pulmonologist/Medical Specialist. 
19. Bronchitis. History of repeated attacks of cough/wheezing/bronchitis may be manifestations 
of chronic bronchitis or other chronic pathology of the respiratory tract.  Such cases will be assessed 
unfit and will be subjected to detailed evaluation with appropriate investigations at the time of appeal 
by Pulmonologist/Medical Specialist.  
20. Bronchial Asthma. History of repeated attacks of bronchial asthma/wheezing/ allergic rhinitis 
will be a cause for rejection. 
 
21. Radiographs of the Chest. Definite radiological evidence of disease of the lungs, mediastinum 
and pleurae are criteria for declaring the candidate unfit.   
 
22. Thoracic Surgery. Candidate with history of any major surgery of the thorax will be considered 
unfit.  
Gastrointestinal System 
 
23. Head to toe examination.  Presence of any sign of liver cell failure (e.g. loss of hair, 
parotidomegaly, spider naevi, gynaecomastia, testicular atrophy, flapping tremors etc) and any 
evidence of malabsorption (pallor, nail and skin changes, an gular cheilitis, pedal edema) will entail 
rejection.  
 
36 
 
 
24. Gastro-Duodenal Disabilities. Any past surgical procedure involving partial or total loss of an 
organ (other than vestigial organs/gall bladder) will entail rejection. 
25. Diseases of the Liver.   If past history of jaundice is noted or any abnormality of the liver 
function is suspected, full investigation is required for assessment.  Candidates suffering from viral 
hepatitis or any other form of jaundice will be rejected. Such candidates can be decl ared fit after a 
minimum period of 6 months has elapsed provided there is full clinical recovery; HBV and HCV status 
are both negative and liver functions are within normal limits. History of recurrent jaundice and 
hyperbilirubinemia of any nature is unfit. 
26. Disease of the Spleen. Candidates who have undergone partial/ total splenectomy are unfit, 
irrespective of the cause for operation. 
27. Anterior abdominal wall EPID including femoral hernia.  
27.1.  Fit. After 24 weeks of surgery (open as well as lap aroscopic) provided there is no 
recurrence or post-op complications.  
27.2.    Unfit.  
27.2.1   All current or operated cases of incisional hernia. 
27.2.2.  All cases of current anterior abdominal wall hernia.   
Inguinal Hernia.  
27.3.  FIT. After 01 year of hernia repair surgery (open as well as laparoscopic) provided 
there is no recurrence or post-op complications.  
27.4. Unfit. All cases of current inguinal hernia.

(except appendicectomy through right iliac fossa incision, refer par 36.2) will be considered fit after 24 
weeks provided there is no potential f or any recurrence of the underlying pathology, no evidence of 
incisional hernia and the condition of the abdominal wall musculature is good.

Endocrine System. 
 
59. Any history suggestive of endocrine disorders will be a cause for rejection. 
 
60. Clinical Examination. Any clinical evidence of endocrine disease will be unfit.   
 
42 
 
 
61. All cases of thyroid swelling are unfit. Fitness of such cases will be decided during appeal

Dermatological System. 
 
63. Relevant History and Examination . Candidates who give history of sexual exposure to a 
Commercial Sex Worker (CSW) and have evidence of healed penile sore in the form of a scar must 
be declared permanently unfit, even in abse nce of an overt STD, as these candidates are likely 
‘repeaters’ with similar indulgent promiscuous behaviour.    
 
64. Assessment of Diseases of the Skin.  Acute non -exanthematous and non -communicable 
diseases, which ordinarily run a temporary course, need n ot be a cause of rejection.  Diseases of a 
trivial nature, and those, which do not interfere with general health or cause incapacity, do not entail 
rejection. 
 
65. Certain skin conditions are apt to become active and incapacitating under tropical condition s. 
An individual is unsuitable for service if he has a definite history or signs of chronic or recurrent skin 
disease. Some of such conditions are described below:- 
 
66. Palmoplantar Hyperhydrosis. Some amount of Palmoplantar Hyperhydrosis is physiological, 
considering the situation that recruits face during medical examination. However, candidates with 
significant Palmoplantar Hyperhydrosis should be considered unfit. 
 
67. Acne vulgaris Mild (Grade I) acne consisting of few comedones or papules, localized only to 
the face may be acceptable. However, moderate to severe degree of acne (nodulocystic type with or 
without keloidal scarring) or involving the back should be considered unfit.  
 
68. Palmoplantar Keratoderma  Any degree of palmoplantar keratoderma manifesting with 
hyperkeratotic and fissured skin over the palms, soles and heels should be considered unfit.  
 
69. Ichthyosis vulgaris Ichthyosis involving the upper and lower limbs, with evident dry, scaly, 
fissured skin should be considered unfit. Mild xerosis (dry skin) could be considered fit.  
 
70. Candidates having any keloid should be considered unfit.  
 
71. Clinically evident onychomycosis of finger and toe -nails should be declared unfit, especially if 
associated with nail dystrophy. Mi ld degree of distal discoloration involving single nail without any 
dystrophy may be acceptable.  
 
72. Giant congenital melanocytic naevi, greater than 10 cm should be considered unfit, as there is 
a malignant potential in such large sized naevi.  
 
73. Single corns/ Warts/ Callosities will be considered fit, three months after successful treatment 
and no recurrence. However, candidates with multiple warts/ corns/ callosities on palms and soles or 
diffuse palmoplantar mosaic warts, large callosities on press ure areas of palms and soles should be 
rejected.  
 
74. Psoriasis is a chronic skin condition known to relapse and/or recur and hence should be 
considered unfit.  
 
 
43 
 
75. Vitiligo. Those having vitiligo must be made unfit. On appeal, segmental vitiligo under t he 
covered parts may be accepted. 
 
76. A history of chronic or recurrent episodes of skin infections will be cause for rejection. Folliculitis 
or sycosis barbae from which there has been complete recovery may be considered fit. 
 
77. Individuals who have chronic or frequently recurring episodes of a skin disease of a serious or 
incapacitating nature e.g. eczema are to be assessed as permanently unfit and rejected. 
  
78. Any sign of Leprosy will be a cause for rejection. All peripheral nerves should be examined for 
any thickness of the nerves and any clinical evidence suggestive of leprosy is a ground for rejection.   
 
79. Naevus depigmentosus and Beckers naevus may be considered fit. Intradermal naevus, 
vascular naevi are to be made unfit.   
 
80. Pityriasis Versicolor is to be made unfit. They can be made fit on appeal, if completely treated. 
 
81. Any fungal infection of any part of the body will be unfit. They can be made fit on appeal, if 
completely treated. 
82. Scrotal Eczema may be considered fit on recovery. 
 
83. Canities (premature graying of hair) may be considered fit if mild in nature and no systemic 
association is seen. 
 
84. Intertrigo may be considered fit on recovery. 
 
85. All STDs are unfit. 
86.  Scabies may be considered fit only on recovery.  
 
87.  Alopecia areata single and small (<2 cm in diameter) lesion on scalp can be accepted. However 
if multiple, involving other areas or having scarring, the candidate should be rejected. 
 
88. Gynaecomastia: Candidates to be considered fit after 12 weeks of post-operative period if: - 
88.1. There is a well healed surgical wound with no residual disease. 
88.2. No Post Operative complication. 
88.3. Surgical scar should be sufficiently matured and unlikely to cause any problems during 
military training. 
88.4. Normal general physical examination. 
88.5. Endocrine workup is normal 
89. Polymazia Candidates to be considered fit after 12 weeks of Post-Operative period if there is 
no Post Operative complication with a well healed surgical wound and no residual disease. 
 
Musculoskeletal System and Physical Capacity 
 
90. Spinal Conditions: Past medical history of disease or injury of the spine or sacroiliac joints, 
either with or without objective signs, which has prevented the candidate from successfully following 
a physically active life, is a cause for rejection for commissioning. History of recurrent lumbago/ spinal 
fracture/ prolapsed intervertebral disc and surgical treatment for these conditions will entail rejection. 
91. Clinical Examination. Normal thoracic kyphosis and cervical/ lumbar lordosis are barely 
noticeable and not associated with pain or restriction of movement.  
 
44 
 
91.1. If clinical examination reveals restriction of spine movements, d eformities, tenderness 
of the spine or any gait abnormalities, it will be considered unfit. 
91.2.  Gross kyphosis, affecting military bearing/ restricts full range of spinal movements 
and/or expansion of chest is unfit. 
91.3.  When scoliosis is noticeable or any pathological condition of the spine is suspected, 
radiographic examination of the appropriate part of the spine needs to be carried out. 
Scoliosis is unfit, if deformity persists on full flexion of the spine, when associated with 
restricted range of spine movements or when due to an underlying pathological cause.  
91.4.  Spina Bifida. The following markers should be looked for, on clinical examination and 
corroborated with radiological evaluation:-  
91.4.1.   Congenital defects overlying the spine eg, hypertrichosis, skin dimpling, 
haemangioma, pigmented naevus or dermal sinus.  
91.4.2.   Presence of lipoma over spine.  
91.4.3.   Palpable spina bifida. 
91.4.4.   Abnormal findings on neurological examination. 
 92. Castellvi Classification for Lumbosacral Transitional Vertebra (LSTV). 
 
  
  
Castellvi Classification for LSTV 
 
92.1. Type I. Enlarged and dysplastic transverse process (at least 19 mm in width in 
craniocaudal dimension).  
 
  92.1.1.  I a. Unilateral. 
 
92.1.2. I b. Bilateral.  
 
92.2. Type II. Pseudoarticulation of the transverse process and sacrum with incomplete 
lumbarisation/sacralistion (enlargement of the transverse process with pseudoarthrosis). 
 
92.2.1. II a. Unilateral. 
 
92.2.2. II b. Bilateral. 
 
92.3. Type III. Transverse process fuses with the sacrum and there is complete 
lumbarisation or sacralisation (enlarged transverse process with complete fusion). 
 
92.3.1. III a. Unilateral. 
 

 
45 
 
92.3.2. III b. Bilateral. 
92.4. Type IV. Type II on one side and type III on the contralateral side. 
 
93. Spinal Conditions Unfit for Air Force Duties (Both Flying and Ground Duties) 
93.1. Congenital/Developmental Anomalies. 
 
  93.1.1. Wedge Vertebra. 
 
  93.1.2. Hemivertebra. 
 
  93.1.3.  Anterior Central Defect. 
 
93.1.4. Cervical Ribs (Unilateral/Bilateral) with demonstrable neurological or 
circulatory deficit. 
 
93.1.5. Spina Bifida. All types are unfit except in sacrum and LV5 (if completely 
sacralised). 
 
93.1.6. Loss of Cervical Lordosis with neurological deficit.  
93.1.7. Assessment of Scoliosis. Idiopathic scoliosis upto 10 degrees for Lumbar 
Spine and 15 degrees for Dorsal Spine will be acceptable provided:- 
 
93.1.7.1. Individual is asymptomatic. 
 
93.1.7.2. No history of trauma to spine. 
 
93.1.7.3 No chest asymmetry/shoulder imbalance or pelvic obliquity in the 
lumbar spine. 
 
93.1.7.4. There is no neurological deficit. 
 
93.1.7.5. No congenital anomaly of the spine. 
 
93.1.7.6. There is absence of syndromic features. 
 
93.1.7.7. ECG is normal. 
 
93.1.7.8. No deformity exists on full flexion of the spine. 
 
93.1.7.9. No restriction of range of movements 
 
93.1.7.10 No organic defect causing structural abnormality.  
 
  93.1.8. Atlanto-occipital and Atlanto-axial anomalies. 
 
93.1.9. Incomplete block vertebra at any level. 
 
93.1.10. Complete block vertebra at more than one level. (Single level is 
acceptable. Annotation is to be made in AFMSF-2). 
 
93.1.11. Lumbosacral Transitional Vertebra (LSTV) . Unilateral sacralisation or 
lumbarisation (complete or incomplete) and B ilateral incomplete sacralisation or 
lumbarisation (LSTV- Castellvi Type II a and b, III a and IV).  
 
46 
 
 
Bilateral Complete Sacralisation of LV5 and Bilateral Complete Lumbarisation of SV1, 
LSTV Castellvi Type III b, Type I a and b are acceptable (Annotation is to be made in 
AFMSF-2). 
 
93.1.12. Spondylolysis/Spondylolisthesis. 
 
93.1.13. Intervertebral Disc Prolapse. 
 
93.1.14. Schmorl’s Nodes at more than one level. 
  
93.2. Traumatic Conditions 
 
  93.2.1. Spondylolysis/ Spondylolisthesis 
 
  93.2.2. Compression fracture of vertebra 
 
  93.2.3. Intervertebral Disc Prolapse 
 
  93.2.4.           Schmorl’s Nodes at more than one level 
 
93.3. Infective 
 
93.3.1.  Tuberculosis and other Granulomatous disease of spine (old or active) 
 
  93.3.2. Infective Spondylitis 
 
93.4. Autoimmune 
 
  93.4.1. Rheumatoid Arthritis and allied disorders 
 
  93.4.2. Ankylosing spondylitis 
 
93.4.3. Other rheumatological disorders of spine e.g Polymyositis, SLE and 
Vasculitis 
 
93.5. Degenerative 
 
  93.5.1. Spondylosis 
 
  93.5.2. Degenerative Joint Disorders 
 
  93.5.3. Degenerative Disc Disease 
 
  93.5.4. Osteoarthrosis/ osteoarthritis 
 
  93.5.5. Scheuerman’s Disease (Adolescent Kyphosis) 
 
93.6. Any other spinal abnormality, if so considered by the specialist. 
 
Conditions affecting the assessment of upper limbs   
94. Amputations and Deformities of Upper limbs. Deformities of the upper limbs or their 
parts will be cause for rejection. Candidate with an amputation of a limb or any part of limb including 
fingers will not be accepted for entry.  
95. Fingers and Hands. Deformities and limitations to movements will be considered unfit.   
 
47 
 
95.1. Polydactyly. Can be declared fit 12 weeks post - operative, if there is no bony 
abnormality on radiograph, wound is well healed, scar is supple and there is no evidence of 
neuroma on clinical examination. 
95.2. Simple Syndactyly. Can be declared fit 12 weeks post -operative, if there is no 
bony abnormality on radiograph, wound is healed, scar is supple and webspace is satisfactory. 
95.3. Complex syndactyly. Unfit. 
95.4. Hyperextensible finger joints. All candidates shal

Exams » Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment... The High Court of Orissa has announced the Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 for 33 Group-C vacancies under Advertisement No. 06 of 2026. The online application process will begin on 13 November 2026 and continue until 7 December 2026. Candidates seeking Odisha High Court jobs can check the eligibility criteria, vacancy details, application dates, selection process, salary and other important information below. Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026: Overview The recruitment will be conducted by the High Court of Orissa, Cuttack, under Advertisement No. 06/2026 dated 11 November 2026. Candidates appointed to these posts will receive a salary under Level 7 of the Pay Matrix. Particulars Details Organisation High Court of Orissa, Cuttack Recruitment Name Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 Advertisement Number 06/2026 Post Name Junior Stenographer (Group-C) Total Vacancies 33 Job Location Cuttack, Odisha Application Mode Online Notification Date 11 November 2026 Application Start Date 13 November 2026, 10:00 AM Last Date to Apply 7 December 2026, 11:59 PM Educational Qualification Bachelor’s Degree Shorthand Speed 80 WPM Typewriting Speed 40 WPM Selection Process English Test, Computer Application Test and Skill Test Pay Scale ₹25,500–₹81,100 Pay Level Level 7 Official Website orissahighcourt.nic.in Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Notification 2026 PDF The High Court of Odisha has issued the official notification for 33 Junior Stenographer vacancies. It contains information about educational qualifications, age limits, reservation, examination fees, selection stages, skill test requirements and application instructions. Candidates should read the advertisement carefully before applying to ensure they meet all the prescribed conditions. Download Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Notification 2026 PDF Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026: Important Dates The Odisha High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 application date and other important events are listed below. Candidates should keep track of the registration schedule to avoid missing the deadline. Event Date and Time Notification Release Date 11 November 2026 Online Application Starts 13 November 2026, 10:00 AM Last Date to Apply Online 7 December 2026, 11:59 PM Examination Date To be announced Odisha High Court Junior Stenographer Vacancy 2026: Category-Wise Posts A total of 33 Junior Stenographer vacancies have been announced across different categories. The recruitment includes reserved posts for Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST) and Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBC) candidates. The category-wise vacancy distribution is given below. Category Total Vacancies Women Vacancies UR 11 4 SEBC 1 – ST 12 4 SC 9 3 Total 33 11 Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Apply Online 2026 The online application process for Odisha High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 will begin on 13 November 2026 at 10:00 AM. Eligible candidates can submit their application forms through the official website until 7 December 2026 at 11:59 PM. Candidates can access the direct application link provided below. Apply Online for Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 (Link Active Soon) Odisha High Court Stenographer Application Fee 2026 Candidates applying for the recruitment must pay an examination fee of ₹500. The fee is non-refundable and non-adjustable. SC, ST and Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) candidates are exempted from payment. Category Examination Fee General/Other Eligible Candidates ₹500 SC Exempted ST Exempted PwBD Exempted How to Apply for Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026? Candidates can apply online through the official website of the High Court of Odisha by following these steps: Visit the official website. Open the Recruitment Corner and select the Examination Portal. Click on Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 (Advertisement No. 06/2026). Complete the registration process. Fill in the application form with the required details. Upload the photograph, signature and necessary certificates. Pay the application fee, if applicable. Submit the form and download a copy for future reference. Candidates should check all details carefully before submitting the application form. Documents Required for Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026 Candidates must keep the following documents ready while filling out the online application form under Advertisement No. 06/2026. Document Purpose Class 10th Certificate Date of Birth Proof Bachelor’s Degree Certificate Educational Qualification Computer Certificate Computer Knowledge Shorthand and Typewriting Certificate Technical Qualification Character Certificates Character Verification Passport-Size Photograph Identification Signature Application Verification Aadhaar Card Identity Proof Caste Certificate Category Reservation, if applicable Disability Certificate PwBD Candidates, if applicable Discharge Certificate Ex-Servicemen, if applicable Gazette Notification and Newspaper Publication Name Change, if applicable Odisha High Court Junior Stenographer Eligibility Criteria 2026 Candidates must meet the prescribed educational qualification, technical skills and age requirements to apply for Junior Stenographer posts. The eligibility conditions are explained below. Educational Qualification Applicants must fulfil the following educational and technical requirements: A Bachelor’s Degree in any discipline from a recognised university. Shorthand speed of at least 80 words per minute. Typewriting speed of at least 40 words per minute. Adequate knowledge of Computer Applications. Candidates must possess certificates issued by recognised institutions to support their shorthand and typewriting qualifications. Age Limit The minimum and maximum age requirements will be calculated as on 12 November 2026. Particulars Details Minimum Age Above 21 years Maximum Age 42 years Age Calculation Date 12 November 2026 Date of Birth Range Not earlier than 12 November 1984 and not later than 11 November 2005 The date of birth mentioned in the High School Certificate or equivalent certificate issued by the concerned Board or Council will be considered valid proof of age. Age Relaxation Candidates belonging to reserved categories and other eligible groups will receive relaxation in the upper-age limit as per the recruitment rules. Category Upper-Age Relaxation SC 5 Years ST 5 Years SEBC (Non-Creamy Layer) 5 Years Women Candidates 5 Years PwBD (40% to 50% Disability) 10 Years PwBD belonging to SC/ST/SEBC 15 Years Ex-Servicemen As per Government Rules Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Selection Process 2026 The selection process consists of three stages to assess candidates’ English language knowledge, computer skills and stenography abilities. The stages are: Qualifying Test in English: Candidates must appear for a written examination carrying 100 marks. Only those securing the prescribed qualifying marks will proceed to the next stage. Computer Application Test: Shortlisted candidates will appear for a 100-mark computer test. This stage is qualifying in nature. Shorthand and Typewriting Skill Test: Candidates who qualify in the computer test will be called for the final skill test. The final merit list will be prepared based on the marks obtained in the Skill Test. Candidates will be arranged in descending order of marks, and separate merit lists will be prepared for the General and reserved categories. Candidates should also practise previous year papers to understand the question pattern and improve their preparation. They can refer to the OSSC Junior Stenographer Previous Year Question Papers PDF for practice. Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Exam Pattern 2026 The selection examination will be conducted in three stages: an English written test, a Computer Application Test and a Shorthand and Typewriting Skill Test. Candidates must qualify in each stage to move to the next round. Stage 1: English Written Test The first stage carries 100 marks, and candidates will get 1 hour and 30 minutes to complete the paper. Subject Marks Essay Writing in English 20 Odia to English Translation 20 English to Odia Re-translation 20 English Grammar 40 Total 100 Time Duration 90 Minutes Qualifying Marks: General category: 35% SC/ST categories: 30% Stage 2: Computer Application Test Candidates who qualify in the English test will appear for the Computer Application Test. It carries 100 marks and is qualifying in nature. Test Marks Duration Computer Theory 50 30 Minutes Practical Computer Test 50 30 Minutes Total 100 60 Minutes Candidates must score at least 50% marks to qualify for the next stage. Topics: MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, MS Access, Internet Operations and File Uploading/Downloading. Stage 3: Shorthand and Typewriting Skill Test Candidates qualifying in the Computer Application Test will appear for the final Skill Test. They will have to take English dictation in shorthand and type the passage on a computer. Particulars Details Dictation Passage 400 Words Shorthand Speed 80 Words Per Minute Dictation Time 5 Minutes Typing Speed 40 Words Per Minute Transcription Time 10 Minutes Total Marks 100 Marks per Correct Word 0.25 Important: Candidates can make mistakes or omissions up to 10% of the total dictated words. Exceeding this limit will lead to disqualification. Final Merit List: The merit list will be prepared based on the marks obtained in the Shorthand and Typewriting Skill Test. Odisha High Court Junior Stenographer Syllabus 2026 The Odisha High Court Junior Stenographer examination covers English, Computer Applications, Shorthand and Typewriting. The main topics for each stage are given below. Examination Stage Syllabus / Topics English Test English Essay, Odia to English Translation, English to Odia Re-translation and English Grammar Computer Application Test MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint, MS Access, Internet Operations, File Uploading and Downloading Skill Test English Shorthand Dictation, Transcription and Typewriting Candidates preparing for the examination can also refer to the detailed OSSC Junior Stenographer Syllabus to understand the subject-wise topics and plan their preparation accordingly. Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Salary 2026 Candidates selected through the Cuttack High Court Recruitment 2026 will receive the prescribed salary under Level 7 of the Odisha Pay Matrix. Particulars Details Post Name Junior Stenographer Pay Level Level 7 Pay Scale ₹25,500–₹81,100 Pay Rules ORSP Rules, 2017 Additional Benefits Dearness Allowance and other applicable allowances Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026: FAQs Q1. How many vacancies are announced under Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026? Ans. 33 Junior Stenographer vacancies. Q2. When does the application process start? Ans. 13 November 2026. Q3. Q14. What is the application date for Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026? Ans. The online application process starts on 13 November 2026 and closes on 7 December 2026. Q4. What is the educational qualification required? Ans. Bachelor’s Degree from a recognised university. Q5. What is the age limit for Orissa High Court Junior Stenographer Recruitment 2026? Ans. Above 21 years and up to 42 years. Q6. What is the Junior Stenographer salary? Ans. ₹25,500–₹81,100 under Level 7. Q7. What is the application fee? Ans. ₹500. SC, ST and PwBD candidates are exempted. Q8. What shorthand and typing speed is required? Ans. 80 WPM shorthand and 40 WPM typing. Q9. What is the selection process? Ans. English Test, Computer Application Test and Skill Test. Q10. Is the Computer Application Test qualifying? Ans. Yes, candidates need at least 50% marks. Q11. How many words are included in the Skill Test? Ans. 400 words. Q12. How is the final merit list prepared? Ans. Based on Skill Test marks. Q13. What is the official website for Odisha High Court Recruitment 2026? Ans. The official website is orissahighcourt.nic.in. Exams » Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment... Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI), New Delhi, has released the Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment 2026 Notification (Advertisement No. 01/2026-27 NT) to recruit for various non-teaching positions. According to the provided notification details, the recruitment covers 85 vacancies across different departments, including the Registrar’s Office, Finance & Accounts Office, Building & Construction Department, Library, Health Centre and other university departments. The online application process starts on 12 November 2026, and eligible candidates can submit their applications up to 11 December 2026. Candidates must also send a hard copy of the application form along with self-attested documents by 21 December 2026. Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Notification 2026 Out The official notification of Jamia Millia Islamia Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026 contains complete details regarding 85 vacancies across 35 posts, including post-wise vacancy distribution, educational qualifications, age limits, work experience, application fees, selection process and application procedure. Candidates can check the department-wise vacancies and eligibility requirements before submitting their applications. The notification also provides important instructions regarding online application submission and mandatory hard copy submission along with supporting documents. Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment 2026- Notification PDF Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment 2026 Out Check the key recruitment details in the overview table below. Particulars Details Organization Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI) Recruitment Name JMI Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026 Advertisement No. 01/2026-27 (NT) Total Vacancies 85 Post Name Non-Teaching Posts Job Location New Delhi Application Mode Online + Hard Copy Selection Process Written Test/Skill Test/Trade Test/Interview Official Website www.jmi.ac.in Important Dates The online application process for JMI Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026 begins on 12 November 2026. Candidates must complete the online form and submit the required hard copy within the prescribed deadlines. Event Date Notification Release Date 10 November 2026 Online Application Start Date 12 November 2026 Online Application Last Date 11 December 2026 Hard Copy Submission Last Date 21 December 2026 Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Vacancy 2026: Post-Wise Details Jamia Millia Islamia has announced 85 vacancies for 35 different non-teaching posts across various university departments. Candidates can check the post-wise vacancy distribution in the table below. Post Name No. of Vacancies Assistant Registrar 03 Section Officer 04 Assistant 03 Upper Division Clerk (UDC) 10 Hindi Typist 02 Urdu Typist 04 Land Record Superintendent 01 Land Record Keeper 01 Internal Audit Officer (Deputation) 01 Assistant Finance Officer 02 Accountant 02 Superintendent Engineer (Civil) 01 Executive Engineer (Civil) (Deputation) 01 Electrician 05 Plumber 03 Carpenter 05 Whitewasher 02 Mason 01 Wireman 03 Beldar 06 Mate 04 Professional Assistant 01 Garden Superintendent 01 Garden Supervisor 02 Horticulture Assistant 02 Pharmacist 03 Dresser 02 Medical Attendant 01 Photographer 01 Store Keeper 01 Chair Side Attendant 03 Video Editor 01 Caretaker 01 Cook 01 Sanitary Inspector 01 Total 85 What Is The Application Fee? Candidates applying for Jamia Millia Islamia Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026 must pay the application fee according to their post group and category. The application fee is non-refundable. SC/ST candidates will receive a 50% concession, while PwBD (Divyangjan) candidates are exempted from the application fee upon submitting a valid certificate. Group Category Application Fee Group A Positions (Pay Level 10 and above) UR/OBC ₹1,000 SC/ST ₹500 PwBD (Divyangjan) Nil Group B and C Positions (Pay Level 7 and below) UR/OBC ₹700 SC/ST ₹350 PwBD (Divyangjan) Nil Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Apply Online Candidates who meet the prescribed eligibility criteria can submit their applications for Jamia Millia Islamia Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026 through the university’s official recruitment portal. Applicants must complete the registration, fill in the application form, upload the required documents and pay the applicable fee before the deadline. Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment 2026- Apply Link After submitting the online form, candidates must also send a printed copy with self-attested documents to the university by 21 December 2026. How to Apply Online for Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment 2026? Candidates can follow the steps given below to complete the online application process for Jamia Millia Islamia Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026: Visit the official recruitment portal at jobs.jmi.ac.in. Find the link for Advt. No. 01/2026-27 (NT). Select the post for which you want to apply and click on the Apply option. Complete the registration process using the required details. Fill out the online application form with personal, educational and experience details. Upload the required photograph, signature and supporting documents. Pay the application fee according to your category and post group. Review all the details carefully and submit the application form. Download and take a printout of the submitted application form on A4-size paper. Affix your signature, paste a recent photograph and attach self-attested copies of the required documents. FAQs: Jamia Millia Islamia Non Teaching Recruitment 2026 Q1. How many vacancies are announced under Jamia Millia Islamia Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026? A total of 85 vacancies have been announced across 35 different non-teaching posts. Q2. When was the Jamia Millia Islamia Recruitment 2026 notification released? The official notification was released on 10 November 2026 under Advertisement No. 01/2026-27 (NT). Q3. When will the online application process start? The online application process starts on 12 November 2026. Q4. What is the last date to apply online for JMI Recruitment 2026? The last date for submitting the online application form is 11 December 2026. Q5. What is the last date for hard copy submission? Candidates must submit their printed application form along with supporting documents by 21 December 2026. Q6. What is the educational qualification required for JMI Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026? The required qualification ranges from High School and Intermediate to Graduation, Post-Graduation, ITI and professional degrees, depending on the post. Q7. What is the age limit for Jamia Millia Islamia Non-Teaching posts? The maximum age limit for most posts is 40 years. Certain deputation-based positions have a preferred age limit below 56 years. Q8. What is the application fee for JMI Recruitment 2026? For Group A posts, the fee is ₹1,000 for UR/OBC and ₹500 for SC/ST candidates. For Group B and C posts, it is ₹700 for UR/OBC and ₹350 for SC/ST candidates. PwBD candidates are exempted. Q9. What is the selection process for Jamia Millia Islamia Recruitment 2026? Candidates may be selected through a written examination, skill test, trade test and/or interview, depending on the post. Q10. Can candidates apply for more than one post? Yes, candidates can apply for multiple posts, but a separate application form must be submitted for each post. Q11. Is hard copy submission mandatory for JMI Non-Teaching Recruitment 2026? Yes, submission of the printed application form with self-attested supporting documents is mandatory. Q12. Where can candidates apply online for Jamia Millia Islamia Recruitment 2026? Candidates can submit their applications through the official recruitment portal: https://jobs.jmi.ac.in/. Q13. Are candidates who applied under the previous advertisement required to apply again? Yes, candidates who previously applied under Advertisement No. 02/2025-26 (NT) for posts marked with an asterisk (*) must apply afresh. However, they are exempted from the application fee if they submit the prescribed proof of their previous application. items.doc_text: Exams » DSSSB MTS Apply Online 2026 The Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) has activated the online application process for DSSSB MTS Recruitment 2026 under Advertisement No. 06/2026. A total of 1,075 Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) vacancies have been announced in various departments of the Delhi Government, including MTS General Duty and MTS Aaya (Female) posts. Eligible candidates can submit their application forms online from 12 November 2026 to 11 December 2026 through the official application portal. DSSSB MTS Apply Online 2026: Overview The recruitment offers an opportunity for eligible candidates seeking government jobs in Delhi. Candidates can check the important recruitment details in the table below. Particulars Details Recruiting Organisation Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) Post Name Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) Advertisement No. 06/2026 Total MTS Vacancies 1,075 Application Mode Online Application Start Date 12 November 2026 Last Date to Apply 11 December 2026 Qualification 10th Pass / As per post Age Limit 18–27 Years Salary ₹18,000–₹56,900 Selection Process Computer-Based Examination Job Location Delhi Official Website dsssb.delhi.gov.in Delhi MTS Apply Online 2026: Direct Link The DSSSB MTS Online Application process has started on 12 November 2026 at the official website. Eligible candidates can submit their application forms for 1,075 MTS vacancies through the online portal at dsssbonline.nic.in. Applicants must complete the registration, upload the required documents and pay the application fee, if applicable. The last date to apply online is 11 December 2026. DSSSB MTS 2026 Apply Online – Apply Link How to Apply for Delhi DSSSB MTS 2026? Candidates can follow these steps to apply: Visit the official DSSSB application portal. Complete the One-Time Registration (OTR) process. Log in using your registration credentials. Select Advertisement No. 06/2026 and MTS Post Code 810/26. Fill in the required personal and educational details. Upload the photograph, signature and other required documents. Pay the application fee, if applicable. Review all the details and submit the application form. Download and print the final submitted application for future reference. Documents Required for DSSSB MTS Application Form Candidates should keep the following documents ready before filling out the online application form: Class 10th marksheet and certificate Aadhaar Card or other valid identity proof Recent passport-size photograph Scanned signature Category certificate (if applicable) Educational qualification documents Valid email ID and mobile number Other documents required as per the notification DSSSB MTS Eligibility Criteria 2026 Candidates must fulfil the educational qualification and age requirements specified by DSSSB to apply for the MTS vacancies. Educational Qualification Candidates should have passed Class 10 (Matriculation) or an equivalent examination from a recognised board. However, applicants should check the detailed advertisement for any additional or post-specific qualification requirements before applying. Age Limit The prescribed age limit for DSSSB MTS posts is generally 18 to 27 years, calculated as of 11 December 2026. Reserved category candidates will receive upper-age relaxation according to the applicable Delhi Government rules. What is the Application Fee? Candidates must pay the prescribed application fee while submitting the online application form. The category-wise fee details are given below. Category Application Fee General / OBC / EWS (Male) ₹100 Female Candidates Nil SC / ST Candidates Nil PwBD Candidates Nil Ex-Servicemen Nil DSSSB MTS Selection Process 2026 The selection of candidates for Multi-Tasking Staff posts will be based on a One-Tier General Computer-Based Examination. Candidates who qualify in the examination will be considered for further selection formalities, including document verification, as applicable. FAQs DSSSB MTS 2026 Q1. Is the DSSSB MTS Apply Online 2026 link active ? Yes, the online application link is active from 12 November 2026. Q2. How many vacancies are announced under DSSSB MTS Recruitment 2026? A total of 1,075 MTS vacancies have been announced. Q3. What is the last date to apply for DSSSB MTS Recruitment 2026? The last date to submit the online application form is 11 December 2026. Q4. What is the educational qualification for DSSSB MTS 2026? Candidates generally need to pass Class 10 or possess the prescribed equivalent qualification, subject to the specific post requirements. Q5. What is the age limit for DSSSB MTS Recruitment 2026? The general age limit is 18 to 27 years, with applicable age relaxation for reserved categories. Q6. What is the application fee for DSSSB MTS 2026? The application fee is ₹100 for eligible male General, OBC and EWS candidates. Female, SC, ST, PwBD and Ex-Servicemen candidates are exempted.
